title: If ADF recruitment in PNG isn’t transparent, it will look corrupt | The Strategist
paragraphs: Australia’s recruitment of 100 Papua New Guinean university students and graduates into the Australian Defence Force will almost certainly attract corruption allegations. Canberra needs to begin publicly setting out a transparent, metrics-based selection process before applications open on 16 November.

These are among the most lucrative jobs available to PNG graduates, and most of the thousands of eligible applicants will be rejected. In PNG, an opaque selection process will be assumed to be corrupt, and those narratives will spread across WhatsApp and TikTok faster than Australia can counter them.

And with good reason. Wantok obligations – the kinship ties at the heart of PNG society – will put heavy pressure on anyone with influence over the selection process. Australia should over-communicate its criteria to make clear that Wantok obligations will not in fact make a difference. There must be no public doubt about how candidates are chosen.
